Grandma Lise's Butter Tarts (makes 12)
1/2 cup packed brown sugar
1/2 cup corn syrup
1/4 cup butter, melted
1 egg, beaten
1 tsp vanilla
1/3 cup raisins (optional)
12 unbaked 3 in tart shells
Mix the filling and spoon into shells 2/3 full. Bake at 425°F (220°C) for 12 to 15 minutes until bubbly.
Don't overfill!

Tourtière (serves 8)
1 lb ground pork and 1/2 lb ground beef
1 onion, finely chopped
1 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ground cloves
1 cup water and 1 medium potato, grated
Pastry for a 9 in double-crust pie
Simmer meat, onion, spices and water for 30 min, then stir in the potato. Cool, fill the pie, cut vents and bake at 400°F for 35 to 40 min until golden.
Freezes well for up to 3 months.

Nanaimo Bars, 9 x 9 in pan (24 squares)
Base: 1/2 cup butter, 1/4 cup sugar, 5 tbsp cocoa, 1 egg, 1 1/4 cups graham crumbs, 1 cup coconut, 1/2 cup chopped walnuts
Middle: 1/2 cup butter, 2 tbsp custard powder, 3 tbsp milk, 2 cups icing sugar
Top: 4 oz semi-sweet chocolate melted with 2 tbsp butter
Chill each layer 20 min before adding the next. Cut with a hot knife.

Soupe aux pois / Yellow Pea Soup
2 cups dried yellow peas, soaked overnight
1 ham hock (about 1 1/2 lb)
10 cups water
1 onion, 2 carrots, 2 stalks celery, diced
2 bay leaves, 1 tsp dried savory
Simmer everything for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, stirring now and then. Remove the hock, shred the meat and return it to the pot. Season to taste.
Serves 6 to 8

A Short History of the Harbourfront
Port Carrick grew up around a sawmill built at the mouth of the Carrick River in 1834. By 1871 the town had 6,200 residents, three shipyards and a rail spur to the grain elevators.
The great fire of 12 May 1898 destroyed 41 buildings along Water Street. The stone customs house, finished in 1902, is one of the few landmarks from the rebuilding still standing today.

Protect yourself from the cold
When the wind chill is −28 or colder, exposed skin can freeze in 10 to 30 minutes. Cover your nose, ears, cheeks and fingers.
Dress in layers and keep dry. Wet clothing loses most of its warmth, so change out of damp layers quickly.
Watch for signs of hypothermia: shivering, confusion, slurred speech and drowsiness. Call 911 if someone shows signs of severe hypothermia.

2.3 The Canadian Shield
The Canadian Shield covers roughly half of Canada's land area. Its rocks are among the oldest on Earth, some more than 2.5 billion years old.
Glaciers scraped much of the soil away, leaving thousands of lakes. For this reason farming is limited, but the region is rich in minerals such as nickel, gold and copper.

In the 1920s, ice harvesting was one of Port Carrick's busiest winter trades. Crews cut blocks about 60 cm square and 45 cm thick from the frozen lake, each weighing roughly 150 kg, and stored them in sawdust in icehouses along the shore.

Smoke and carbon monoxide alarms save lives
Ontario law requires a working smoke alarm on every storey of your home and outside all sleeping areas.
Test alarms monthly by pressing the test button. Replace batteries once a year, and replace the whole alarm every 10 years, or as the manufacturer recommends.
Failing to comply can result in a ticket of $360 or a fine of up to $50,000 for individuals.

The 1957 Lakers
Nobody gave the 1957 Lakers much of a chance. They had lost 9 of their first 14 games, and their best defenceman, Ernie Valois, was playing with two cracked ribs.
But on March 22, in front of 3,100 fans packed into an arena built for 2,400, they beat Kingsford 4–3 in double overtime to win the Lakeshore Senior A title. Goalie Walt Kubiak made 46 saves.
The trophy is still on display in the arena lobby.
